title: Chapter 3251 Life is Desire
content:
Sunny had gone on memory journeys with Cassie many times — all the way back from his days of running a Memory shop in Bastion. Each time, he got lost in the trance of her Transcendent Ability, forgetting about time flowing steadily in the real world.

But it was only now that he had to wait for someone else to relive countless memories that he felt how tortuous time truly was. How long did it take to experience an entire life anew? Cassie's power was already miraculous, allowing entire decades to be relived in a matter of hours — days, at most. And yet, Sunny still felt like it wasn't fast enough.

He waited, and waited, and waited, thoughts swarming restlessly in his mind.

He had a lot to think about — an actual god had given a promise to kill Nephis one day, after all. The mysterious core of this Nightmare... he already had a vague suspicion of what it entailed. And if his suspicion was right, then the last trial they had to face would be truly brutal, if not entirely impossible to overcome.

More so than any other impossible trial they had overcome in the past.

But no matter how hard he tried to focus on the looming threat of the Nightmare, wanting to start coming up with possible solutions and preparing himself mentally for future strife, he just could not concentrate. All he could think about was whether Nephis would be able to regain her true personhood in the same way he had. Eventually, Sunny gave up on waiting in front of Cassie's chambers and forced himself to leave. He wandered the Jade Palace for a while, noticing familiar faces from time to time. Friendly company could distract him from worry, but he felt a strong unwillingness to talk to others.

His thoughts were too pressing and chaotic to maintain a conversation.

Mordret was doing... gods knew what. He seemed to have developed a few odd hobbies after spending centuries trying to spy on Nether, all but moving into the library of the Jade Palace and burying himself in various books and scrolls. Whatever Mordret was reading them for was a mystery — after all, he performed most of his research in the depths of his Mirror Domain, safely hidden from view.

Sable, meanwhile, was spending her time with the Jade Queen. They had built rapport at an astonishing speed, and the Jade Queen seemed to like her a lot. Sunny was very surprised by that development, considering that one of them was a young human, while the other was an ancient horror raised personally by the Demon of Dread...

But then again, was it that surprising? Smile of Heaven seemed to be liked by everyone. She had an odd ability to win over and endear everyone she met in a matter of minutes — days, at most. The strangest thing about her, though, was that the source of that ability was entirely mundane, having nothing to do with her Aspect or Attributes.

Sunny avoided both Sable and the Jade Queen, too on edge to keep them company. In the end, he ended up on the walls of the Jade Palace, staring into the distance with a blank expression on his face as he stood motionlessly.

By the time an attendant came to fetch him, a thick layer of snow had already built up on his shoulders.

Sunny turned his head slightly.

"What is it?"

The attendant bowed deeply.

"I was sent to deliver a message, Lord Shadow. Her Majesty, White Abyss, has emerged from the Oracle's chambers."

Finally, a hint of vitality returned to Sunny's eyes... but a hint of anxiety flashed in them, as well.

He remained silent for a moment, then nodded.

"Lead the way."

Soon enough, he arrived in front of an ornate door that led to Neph's own quarters. The corridor was empty, and the attendant also disappeared after showing him the way — it seemed like the Jade Queen, as well as her other guests, were giving him a moment of privacy with his former... present?... partner.

'How thoughtful.'

Sunny remained in front of the door for a few long moments, gathering his courage. The unfeeling, desolate eyes of White Abyss surfaced in his mind, making him grit his teeth tightly.

Had it worked?

Had Nephis been able to remember her former self, were the flames of her soul reignited? Or was she still White Abyss, her original self buried under the weight of eons?

Sunny had experienced hundreds of thousands of lives, hundreds of thousands of deaths. Some of the lives he had lived until the bitter end were short, while some were excruciatingly long.

But Neph's Domain had been composed entirely of humans... so she must have experienced billions of human lives, drowning in the raging ocean of their desires.

Even if human lives were short and fleeting, could her own desire, her own passion have survived in these restless depths?

Finally, taking a deep breath, he raised a hand and knocked on the door.

Then, opening it, he stepped into Neph's chambers.

He found her sitting on the edge of an opulent bed, staring into the window with a distant expression.

For a moment, he could not tell who he was looking at — was it Nephis? Was it White Abyss?

Was it someone entirely new, having inherited parts of both, but resembling neither?

It was only when Nephis turned her head and looked at him that an involuntary sigh of relief escaped from between his lips.

His heart, which felt like it had been stuck in a vice, finally began to beat regularly.

'It's her.'

Nephis... his Nephis. It was unmistakably her.

Her face was just as motionless as it had been when they met on the bridge, and her eyes were still cold and aloof. However, it was the familiar, endearing sort of aloofness he knew so well — one he had been learning to interpret ever since the Forgotten Shore. Yes, Nephis had changed. How could she not, having experienced eons? But her essence was still the same. In fact, it felt as if it had only become more extreme.

Just like Sunny had changed, but remained fundamentally the same.

He remained silent for a moment, trying to compose himself, then asked in a voice that he hoped did not sound nervous:

"How do you feel?"

Nephis did not answer immediately.

She studied him, white sparks glinting in her eyes. Eventually, though, she opened her mouth and said in an even tone:

"Like I woke up from a dream."

Then, the corners of her mouth curled up slightly.

"Only to find myself in a Nightmare."

Sunny tried to hold himself back, but still could not help but smile.

"The usual, then."

He walked over and sat beside her. For a while, the two of them looked at the snowy vista of Ravenheart — the future Ravenheart — together.

Sunny tried to imagine how Nephis felt. She had to be very confused at the moment — just like he had been. The powerful memories of her original life were clashing with the vast depths of the memories she had earned during the Unmaking and throughout the ages of this long, terrifying Nightmare. Her sense of self as Nephis, the last daughter of the Immortal Flame clan, was clashing with the mythical persona of White Abyss, the First Ruler.

After a while, Nephis sighed quietly.

"My mother is alive."

Sunny turned to look at her, hesitated for a moment, and nodded.

She looked at him, as well. Her expression was neutral for a few moments, then slowly creased into a slight frown.

“And what was that about you stuffing her into a doll? Did I remember correctly?"

Sunny blinked a couple of times, his eyes wide, then looked away and cleared his throat.

“What... who said I stuffed her into a doll? She stole that doll! I cherished it a lot, you know!"

From the corner of his eye, he could see Neph's smile widening a little.

After a few moments of silence, she asked, her voice uncharacteristically heavy with reserved emotion:

“Sunny...”

His entire body shivered from the slight rasp in that voice.

“Don't you want to look at me?"

He inhaled deeply, then exhaled. Then, taking another breath once more, he turned to face her.

“Of course, I do. You're the only thing I want to look at."

Nephis smiled.

“Don't you want to touch me?"

As if hypnotized, he raised his hand and caressed her cheek.

The white sparks hidden in the depths of her eyes blazed, turning into dancing flames.

Her voice sounded like a knell, absorbing all of the world.

"Don't you want to kiss me?"

"...Don't you want to embrace me?"

Despite the burden of his Flaw, Sunny did not say anything.

That was not to say that he did not answer, though. He just chose to answer with his actions.

Soon enough, the attendants waiting at the far ends of the corridor outside the guest chambers had to look at each other with awkward expressions.

They let out heavy sighs.

It seemed that their queen was going to have to wait for an audience with the venerable White Abyss for a while longer...
